# Install CDSeq2

## Install from GitHub

Use R 4.1 or newer, a C++ toolchain suitable for R packages, and an internet connection for dependencies. The bundled tutorial was tested with R 4.6.1 and CDSeq2 0.0.0.9000. The [paper benchmark](independent-eqtl.qmd) records a stricter environment for numerical replay.

Run the following in R to install CDSeq2 from [its GitHub repository](https://github.com/kkang7/CDSeq2):

```r
install.packages("remotes")
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("BiocManager")
}
if (!requireNamespace("limma", quietly = TRUE)) {
  BiocManager::install("limma", ask = FALSE, update = FALSE)
}
remotes::install_github("kkang7/CDSeq2")
```

These commands install the Bioconductor dependency `limma` if needed, then install CDSeq2 and its remaining required dependencies from GitHub and CRAN.

## Check the installation

```r
library(CDSeq2)
packageVersion("CDSeq2")
stopifnot(all(c("cdseq2", "prepare_variation_features", "score_variation",
               "train_variation_scorer", "select_variation_profiles") %in%
              getNamespaceExports("CDSeq2")))
help("cdseq2", package = "CDSeq2")
```

## Optional dependencies

| Task | Additional software |
|---|---|
| Run the synthetic tutorial | No packages beyond CDSeq2's dependencies |
| Render or preview this book | Quarto 1.7.32, the version used here |
| Rebuild statistical figures | R; no CDSeq2 inference is run |
| Rebuild the Figure 1 schematic | Python 3.9+, `reportlab`, `pypdfium2` |
| Run the independent eQTL benchmark | BayesPrism and recorded CRAN/Bioconductor dependencies |

Install the benchmark dependencies with `Rscript tools/install_dependencies.R benchmark`. It pins the BayesPrism source commit used in the paper, but does not force all installed dependencies to the recorded versions. Review the benchmark environment table before attempting exact replay.

For source compilation setup, follow the [official R installation manual](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html). Quarto installation is described in the [official Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/).
